Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over This game is best for really young children! I'd say 2-4. My son is almost 4, but he has some learning delays, so this game has proved perfect for him. Most of the games that are sold in stores, like Wal-Mart are still too old for him. I believe in challenging him, but he just doesn't understand them yet. Again, though, this one has proved to be perfect for him. I've already ordered another game from this line, with hopes to add more along.

There's no type of competition with it. There's 6 wooden snails, a race-board, and two dice. You roll the dice and whatever color they land on, you move that colored snail up a space. If both dice land on the same color, you move that colored snail 2 spaces. Sometimes, I had to wonder what the point was! It IS a great learning tool, though. It teaches taking turns, learning colors, and counting. Plus, quality learning time with children is always a good thing.

While I received this one free for review, I honestly would have purchased it. Before I received it, I didn't even know about this line of games. My son has had fun with it, and I'm really glad that it's now part of our game collection.

Overall, I'd say if your child is very young, or has learning delays, or simply likes simple games, this is a great choice. If your child is used to more advanced games, I wouldn't bother with it. There looks to be more advanced, yet still educational games from this line that might be a better choice, though.
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Oh My Gourd! Family Game for Boys & Girls Age 6 & Up - A Fun & Fast Family Game You Can Play Over & Over

text_fidelity_a:
Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi This is a very simple stock market game that is somewhat accessible to younger players. Throughout the game, you'll buy and sell ingredients, complete potions with special abilities, and manipulate a cool little stock market simulation gadget that rolls colored containers down a ramp to indicate value.

The game is very simple, and offers players, in my opinion, a few too many options during their turn. Adults and gamers will find that the ability to sell sets at maximum value to be pretty easy because of the ability to sell not only sets, but individual cards (which allows you to essentially set any price for any set you like). To obtain new ingredients, you can buy from the market, buy from the deck, or swap, or use potion effects. That's a lot of choices to handle, and our little gamer found it to be confusing at first because there were simply too many options. She could identify which cards she wanted, but didn't know whether she should buy, trade or use effects to get them.

All told, this is a good game for youngsters, but there is a learning curve to get good. The number of options can be overwhelming and frustrating at first, but after a few plays, anyone as young as six or eight can probably grasp how to do some of the more complex manipulations. I don't think this will ever be a go-to for an adult game night, but for families, you could do a lot worse than this.

Also, the components are great.
text_fidelity_b: Think Fun Mystic Market Strategy Card Game for 2-4 Players Ages 10 and Up – an Exciting Fast Paced Game Perfect for Both Families and Gamers, Multi

We've got a running game going on for 3 days now, and my Potter expert teenager only has 2 wedges. The pieces are a bit too large for the spaces on the board if two or more are on the same space, but they are quality pieces. The HP wedges actually click into place and are not the drop in kind as in the other games.

text_fidelity_a:
NSI Smithsonian Giant Volcano Kit Small When my 4th child, my 6 yr old daughter, decided she wanted to do a volcano for her science fair project, I inwardly groaned. Having gone the modeling clay and salt dough methods in the past with my older children, I really wasn't up for doing this project again. So, I decided to make life easier and buy a kit from the local craft store. I brought it home, THEN decided to read the reviews on it before we started, as there are often good hints in them. Unfortunately I found this volcano had horrible reviews. No one seemed to have any success with them. I almost took it back, but decided to take a peak at the contents. They were completely different from what had been described by previous viewers, so we took a chance at it. It seems that Smithsonian has paid attention to the reviews and the new contents avoid all the previous problems. Instead of a poorly fitting plastic mold that you have to quickly pour uncooperative gray cement into, there are now 2 large cardboard circles that you use embroidery floss to weave a lava tube to. Sounds complicated, I know, but with an extra hand (I actually used my chin) to hold the lava tube in place during the first half, it really isn't difficult. (Use a knife to ensure the slits in the cardboard are all open before you start. Some of the pegs will have more than one string looped over them- just keep the strings all going vertical.) I then taped the structure down onto a larger piece of foamboard. (Not included.) Then, 2 rolls of plaster impregnated mesh tape are cut into 6 inch strips. You then dip the strips into warm water and drape and smooth them around the structure, overlapping them slightly until the entire volcano is covered. My 6 yr old was able to do this part completely without assistance. The plaster was completely dry by the following day. The result was nice and lightweight. The string structure resulted in vertical groove lines that we liked, because they gave the feel of lava flow lines. In fact, I kinda wish we had intentionally made the grooves a little more prominent. The old kit had no paint and was gray. The new contents include brown and green paints with a little sponge to apply them with. My 6 yr old used a paintbrush instead, and needed additional paint because she also painted the foam board base. The kit also includes a small vial of lava "glow" paint that we have yet to add. There are no longer non-working eruption tablets, either. Instead, you are expected to provide your own coloring, vinegar and baking powder (creates a longer eruption than baking soda, according to the directions). But, we have those on hand and specific amounts and instructions are given, so we expect success when we try it tonight. I don't usually write reviews, but felt I had to so people would know that this kit is no longer such a bust. It's been the easy experience I had hoped for! It's too bad Smithsonian doesn't get a fresh review slate to go with the new and improved contents. (Note: I don't know if the old kits are still out on the market. The box our kit came in looked exactly like the one above, except with a sticker touting the glow paint that it came with.)

Edited to add: We added the glow paint. It isn't much, but is pretty impressive looking when the lights are turned off. The recommended amounts of baking powder and vinegar aren't really enough. It's more of a bubbling effect. The baking powder makes bubbles for a longer period of time, but baking soda has a quicker, more dramatic reaction. The best volcano effect is with a reaction called "elephant toothpaste" using yeast. A google search should get you the amounts needed. Anyways, the kit was great. She had the most beautiful volcano at the science fair. : )

Update: It's 4 yrs later and my youngest child also decided he wanted to do a volcano for the science fair. Remembering this kit, we went ahead and got another one. He's 8 and my 15 yr old assembled the cardboard structure for him. We duct taped it down to a foam board and he plastered the strips on, then painted it and the foam board with his 10 yr old sister and 7 yr old friend. You definitely need more paint and a paint brushes in addition to what is in the kit. They now require a scientific method experiment at the science fair, so we tested a variety of volcano eruption recipes: vinegar+baking soda, vinegar+baking powder, peroxide+yeast+dish soap, mentos+coke, and ketchup+dish soap+baking soda to see what was the best. Based on our results, we created our own recipe: 50 ml dish soap+150ml vinegar+1 T baking soda. Baking soda makes the biggest reaction and is dramatically fast, while the dish soap makes bubbles that last. Note: the above recipe is too big for the volcano which holds only 1/4 c liquid. We'll have to size it down.
text_fidelity_b: NSI Smithsonian Giant Volcano Kit Small

text_fidelity_a: SUSSED The Weird Would You Rather Card Game | Ages: Teens, Adults, Kids 12+ | 110 Cards | for Family, Friends and More | Fantasy Version Played a quick round with my wife and 6-year-old daughter as soon as it arrived.  The game is quick and easy - a scorepad, a deck of cards, and a basic set of rules.  You ask questions, on mostly random subjects, and each of the two guessers attempts to figure out what the third player is going to choose from a set of 3 options.  The vocabulary and topic selection is a little tough for a bright 6-year-old, but a little rewording from Mom and Dad helped her get through it.  Overall, it's a cute idea, but it might get old quickly with only one deck, and it has minimal replay value, as the conversation quickly turns to "I would have chosen..." which is going to deflate your desire to play through multiple times.  There's not as many questions as you'd like to see since each card has 4 questions and that constitutes a round.  I could see a game like this making a nice icebreaker for a corporate team-building retreat or a get-to-know-your-classmates style game, but for a family game, it was good, not great, and not something that we'll likely keep coming back to.

text_fidelity_a: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up This version of Monopoly does not use money! Genius idea for very little children! Even my 4-year-old loved playing. It can be very quick (which was perfect!). I was out before I ever passed Go, haha. Instead of money, this game uses green circles called HP. You gradually lose them all to the “bank” in the middle, but you can get more by passing Go or by landing on a plus-one space or by drawing a particular card. When you land on an available property, it’s yours for free. If you land on an owned property, you have to pay a green HP. Simple. This game is easy to understand, super fun, and quick for the short attention spans of young Fortnite players. Instead of everyone starting on Go, we all started on a homemade Battle Bus, jumping off and landing on whatever space you want. So we all started the game in different areas of the board and all started with a property. That helped the game go faster and was just plain fun to copy Fortnite. My kids have already played this 5 times in 2 days. Great buy! I rate this board game A+.
text_fidelity_b: MONOPOLY: Fortnite Edition Board Game Inspired by Fortnite Video Game Ages 13 & Up

White Mountain Puzzles The Games We Played - 1000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle [[VIDEOID:40e42c7526d4583c84ab24e9bda47318]] I really enjoyed this puzzle. I love games, and especially classic games. And, I love puzzles, too, so this is a great mix of two of my favorite hobbies.

I really like how this is constructed. It's all wrapped in plastic, so there's no dangerous paper flap to cut open on the bottom of the box with a knife, and the puzzle is sealed inside in another bag, which prevents lost pieces. The pieces are thick and fit together well, and I really like the dark green backing that the pieces have. It looks really cool, and it makes it easy to see which pieces are upside down. The border is a graduated red/yellow, which makes it easy to separate out the edge pieces

Probably the reason I liked the puzzle most was that this puzzle makes you think and talk about fun memories, instead of just getting frustrated, trying to put 200 pieces of identical blue sky together, like some puzzles have.

This was a really fun puzzle to put together.

+Extremely high quality construction
+Tons of fun games
+Very fun to put together
+Inspires a lot of enjoyable conversation
+Has just about every game that you can remember from your childhood

Cons:

*Twister, Roulette, Monopoly, Battleship, Risk, Tiddly Winks, Donkey Party, Uno, H. R. Chongker Stuffed Animals Handmade Realistic Black Cat Plush Companion Pet Gifts for Women Birthday Anniversary Cat Lover I've answered a few questions about this, so I will include this right away- this is only a plush (a really nice one)- it has no mechanical parts. It doesn't purr, or "breathe", makes no kitten or cat sounds, and therefore, requires no batteries.

This item was purchased as an "emotional support plushie", if you will. People need companionship, even folks who are no longer able to care for a living pet (or no longer wish to have the heartbreak of losing a real cat).

This fellow can absolutely be mistaken for a real cat at a distance. While being held and stroked, it's close enough to pass for a cat who is less than bunny-soft. The expressions and eyes are amazing, the little toe beans are soft silicone and give a little when squeezed. I couldn't have asked for more detail.

The care that went into creating this plush is evident in the details- from the examples in the pictures and video to those included from customer reviews (and those of the custom plushies are OUTSTANDING, I may have to treat myself to one someday!). It comes in a reusable case (resembling a cat carrier) with a little care booklet and grooming tool.

Personally I wouldn't give this plush to a young child (especially not one of the long-haired ones)- frankly, I'd be worried they'd damage it (squish things in the fur, allow the fur to become matted, color it with markers, cut the whiskers or fur...). Kids can be amazingly accidently destructive at times (we know they don't mean to, it just happens).

For me, the Chongker plush was well worth the price for the comfort it brings. I am quite seriously considering purchasing a custom colored one. I've seen the quality in the base product, and I'm confident in their ability to create good lookalike.

text_fidelity_a:
HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900 I am a solid intermediate (I hesitate to call myself advanced). Put a plane in my hands and I can probably fly it pretty well.

I have had a Night Vapor that I absolutely love to fly when I am too lazy to carry all the gear out to a park. I can fly the Night Vapor around the yard. I wanted something just a little bigger to fly in the small field behind my house. After seeing some videos on YT I could tell this plane can fly nice and slow. I made the mistake of thinking this was a 4 channel airplane when I bought it. I got it home and was a little disappointed when I pulled it out and realized there where no ailerons...until I flew it.

I have to say, this little plane is an excellent little flyer. It literally flies itself. Ultra stable in fast and slow flight. Docile stall tendencies and if you just stop touching the sticks it will roll itself over and be flying straight and level within a second or two. Take off roll is only about 5 or 6 feet if you jump of the power. Landings can be done in about 10-15 feet of concrete if you are good at spot landing. Just remember THIS IS NOT A PLANE FOR WINDY DAYS. As much as it sucks to get a RTF home and not fly it, be patient and wait. Even 5 mph is probably a bit much for this featherweight little plane. Experienced flyers will be able to handle this plane up to 5-8 mph but new guys should wait for calm winds. Since this plane is so light it doesn't really break easy, it just bounces off things. Being inherently dumb I like to do things I probably shouldn't. The result of this is my Champ being bounced off roofs, trees, rocks and pretty much any other object I just can't resist buzzing as close as I can. So far only little scuffs on the foam are the evidence of my wild flying. This little bugger is hard to break!

My Dad is new to RC and as soon as they get another Champ in at the hobby store I am buying him one to learn to fly.

As an experienced flyer I would HIGHLY recommend this for a new flyer or an experienced flyer that wants to have fun in a very big back yard or a small field.

By the way, I still wanted a 4 channel so I went straight back to the hobby store and got a Parkzone T-28 (the ultra micro version that is roughly the same size as the Champ). It is fun and the ailerons allow for more aerobatics but I have to admit the Champ is much more fun in a small field because it is so easy to fly.

I have a lot of airplanes and helis. I can't think of a better plane to learn to fly with. The Night Vapor I mentioned is also super easy to fly but the Champ flies more like the bigger planes so it will make a much better trainer.
text_fidelity_b: HobbyZone Champ RTF, HBZ4900

There isnt anything really historically accurate here as a whole but it really is a fun collection of space stuff.

There are 10 different poses for the figures I got with mulitples of each. All the figures look great, no flashing or deformities. I am sure they are copies of old figures. Giger counter guy, camera guy, radio, briefcase and more.

Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari Hasbro's new Elefun's Snackin Safari Game for children 3 and up has a wonderful concept for fun, if your child has a lot of patience. The game is made for 1 or 2 players. There are two elephant heads with handles connected to a long slinky trunk with a suction cup on the end. Included are 2 home base cards and 13 snack cards. The object of the game is to pick up a snack card with the suction cup, and there are 3 different ways to play the game.

The first way to play is to find the Golden Tutti Fruit Cake and be the winner. The second way is to collect all your matching colors to win and the third way is to get the most pairs of matching snacks to win. It sounds easy enough, until you realize that it takes a lot of patience to bounce the elephant's slinky trunk quickly and hard enough to actually suction a card to it. It could take 6 times or 60 times, as the slinky is a weak plastic one and the small suction cup needs to be pushed on a card to pick it up.

Surprisingly enough, the little ones loved the concept, but after a dozen tries to pick up a card, became frustrated. If Hasbro can tweak this game to make a stronger slinky and stronger suction cup, so the little ones can pick up a card after a few tries, this game would be a big hit. I hope Hasbro reads these reviews and makes this cute game less frustrating, as the kids will really enjoy it!
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Elefun Snackin Safari

Card Game for Kids | Ages 6-12 | Fun, Fast-paced and Easy to Learn | Family Game Night Friendly | a Great Boy or Girl Gift Idea Fairly fun game but card quality is poor for the price. I doubt this is a game to play for hours on end yet.....at the price point I would appreciate brand playing card quality. Is the game bad? I have "dealt" with worse.....there are certainly other card games....even Uno; cheaper, with better card quality but after all....this is a fast slap game. The cards feel cheap, look cheap and shuffle the same. They shuffle in a manegable way but to me this is almost disposable card stock quality. The "art" is non existent with numbers simple written and spelled on the card...colors also do not matter.
Your kids might just toss them on the table and mish mosh them to shuffle them. That will work fine. Slamwich has the excellent card quality and is also a fast easy slap game along this price point. If I had a re-do, I would just stick with Slamwich. Card stock is higher quality and game itself is a little more in depth and kids and adults enjoy a few rounds.

I cannot in good conscience recommend this at 8 dollars or higher. The gameplay itself is simple old fashioned war with a light/slight twist. Number cards....say a 14 verus a 32 dont matter at all (the 32 doesnt take the pile)....it is all about the "slap cards" and "challenege cards"...challenge is where your higher number card played actually counts for once. I DO see that very young kids would enjoy it. I do not see this being a "drinking game" or fun for adults without some extra house rules. Quality is simply subpar for the price. The business is in the USA, the cards and actual game itself are outsourced to China if that matters to you.

Rating is ....average. These are close or are average card size....they have a slick coat. The plain white background quickly picks up color bleed or whatever.....

It is not horrible but just eeks in at "ok" for simple card games. It isnt great and it isnt a big go to except for maybe the 7 year old children set...and the box states...6 plus for age and 2 to 7 people. I say...skip don't smack.

Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll Mattel is always creating a new hair fun Barbie doll, as they know girls love to style, set, color and sometimes even cut their doll's hair. This new Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll offers fun with hair coloring- only in an array of pastel rainbow colors. The doll comes with a color cartridge that includes a row of 5 colors- pink, orange, green, blue and purple. You simply load the hair cartridge into the hair tool and slowly and firmly swipe it onto Barbie's hair where you want the rainbow of colors. The colors come out very pastel looking with the exception of the blue and purple- they are darker. Make sure you do this on an old towel- as it is an inky dye mess, until Barbie's hair has dried from the dye.

Once the rainbow dye has dried, our girls adored braiding the colored hair, and using the hair clips and hair bands to get some really colorful looking hair styles. When the fun wears off from that coloring and they want to re-color a different part of Barbie's hair- get out a bottle of white vinegar and an old towel. You will want to pour some vinegar in a bowl and put the doll's hair that is colored in the bowl, until the color comes out. If you have a problem with the darker purple color like we did, you will want to make a paste of baking soda and vinegar in the bowl and put it on the hair. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes, then take her to the sink and rinse. The color usually all comes out within 5 minutes, but if yours isn't- do it again. When the color is all gone- wash with a dab of shampoo- towel blot dry, brush straight, then let sit until the hair is completely dry. Now you're ready to color again.

This Rainbow Hair Barbie is quite a stiff mannequin- no bendable legs- but she is jointed at the arms, legs and neck. One arm is permanently bent- the other straight. She does have cute hoop earrings, a bracelet, heels, brush, hair accessories and a colorful dress. She is pretty much a stiff mannequin doll that loves to go to the beauty salon for her rainbow streaked hair. This can be fun if you have an old towel and vinegar, so the dye will come out easily for the next coloring. I only wish Mattel would tell you that you will need a towel for the mess and vinegar to easily remove the dye- I only knew the way to easily remove the dye from being a dry-cleaning inspector years ago. The hair coloring is fun, but it would have been nice if she had bendable legs for all the sitting this 4 Star doll will be doing at the hair salon.
text_fidelity_b: Barbie Rainbow Hair Doll

Fisher-Price Disney's Jake and The Never Land Pirates - Jake's Musical Pirate Ship Bucky [Amazon Exclusive] My oldest son turns 4 in just over a week, and he absolutely LOVES this toy! It's one of the few toys that he goes back for again and again.

There are two doors on the ship. One is to the back of the cabin and one is over "tick-tock"(the crocodile) who pops out with the press of a button. These doors come off pretty easily, BUT they pop right back on just as easily. There's also 3 "missiles" that shoot out of the cannon on the front of the boat with the press of a button. These worked great for us, but to be honest, those small pieces get lost pretty quickly. My son usually plays with the ship without those.

My favorite feature is the pegs that are placed ALL over the ship. There are little holes on the bottom of Jake and Skully's feet, so you can place them on the pegs and hold them in place while playing. There's even a little clear bar at the very top of the ship that you can put them on, so it looks like they're flying. I think it's a really cool feature!! I also really like the "rocking" motion of the ship when it moves. It kind of wobbles back and forth to look like it's floating on waves.

My only complaints is the sound, first of all. The music sounds kind of like it's coming from cheap speakers, and I find it annoying. My son loves it and likes to press the buttons to hear the music and phrases. If you really didn't like that feature, the batteries could be taken out. (I haven't resorted to that, but it is an option, since my son knows how to swap the on/off switch). Secondly, I do wish that this set also came with Izzy and Cubby, instead of just Jake and Skully. There are stickers on the side of the boat of Izzy and Cubby to look like they are looking out the window waving. I guess that's an attempt to make up for not having them as figurines. I know that you can buy separate figurines, but I don't know if they have pegs on the bottom of their feet to work with this ship.

Overall, our whole family gives it 2 thumbs up! We all love it, and definitely recommend it.

text_fidelity_a:
Scrabble Turbo Slam My feelings about this product are mixed -- We've long been fans of Scrabble, and thought we'd shake things up a bit by trying a different variation of the game. The Electronic Turbo Slam device, first required (3)- AAA batteries (not included). The device, when slammed has pretty loud sound effects/music, which I found annoying after a short while. I also thought there was too much commotion for me with everyone trying to slap down cards to change the letters, and I wasn't crazy about making just (4) letter words. As an adult, baby boomer, I much prefer the standard game of Scrabble -- quiet, relaxed and educational, and with more word potential.

I can see that this would be a great game for parents to play with young children to help them get interested in learning new words -- I would use it as an educational tool, instead of having them feel pressured to make words at record speed.

On the other hand, the speed and noise factor, would probably appeal to lots of teens. Overall, the game is relatively inexpensive, and worth a try for families who enjoy word faster paced, action filled games.
text_fidelity_b: Scrabble Turbo Slam

Moorebot Scout - Tiny AI Camera Robot for Tech-Minded, Pets/Edlerly Watching/Security/Smart Home/Crawlspace Inspection, 1080P, Auto Patrol, Nightvision, Track Option, Indoor (2023) My office was just moved to a new building that as yet has no cameras inside...Well...Sort of. Now I've got Scout here to take care of business. It's like a Ring doorbell on wheels.

I'm having a lot of fun controlling it manually from home. It connects to the wifi at work and I check in on things using the app. It's working very well and seems to hold a signal about 250kbps. 1080p recordings look fine. For myself, the night vision works a charm. It's clear enough to identify people, and that's all that matters. Plus, driving it around my office while I'm in bed is pretty cool, too.

Battery takes about three hours to charge out of the box and it lasts about 2hr running around the building before it goes back to the base. Most recent firmware update makes that process significantly faster, too. If you've got it on a slick surface, it might have some trouble, but it'll get plugged in eventually. Says battery runs out after an hour using only night vision, but you can set that to automatic in the app.

Around the house, the little noises are kinda neat, but for use as security, that'd be something to disable....except the alarm. That's something to keep on in case you need to scare someone off. Recording all that stuff and saving files to the phone is a plus.

I really like this little guy. It's definitely something you'll have to play around with, but it is a load of fun getting set up.

WOW! Stuff Collection Fantastic Beasts – Newt’s Light Painting Wand – Award Winner! You will open up a huge world of fun with the Wizarding World WW-1024 Harry Potter's Light Painting Wand, Brown. The Harry Potter wand is about 14 inches long with a grainy wood looking black handle and brown wand part that ends with a very bright LED light tip. The wand has a nice feel and weight to it and seems to be made of a strong resin plastic. The wand comes in a lovely window box with directions, customer support information and a bonus app for making your light paintings.

There is a tiny button on the wand’s handle for turning on the LED light which only stays on as long as you hold the button down. The 3 included 1.5 V LR41 batteries are replaceable by opening the handle end with a phillips screwdriver. This is a great thing, as I can see replacing the batteries often, as our kids can’t put this wand down for a minute. For those of you that look forward to some creative light painting, you will want to download the app. Light painting is just photographing a moving light at a longer exposure shutter speed, in the dark, with no flash. You will want the camera on a tripod to get the light design without shaky movement.

In our house, we can’t get the kids to stop playing with the light painting wand long enough for us to try the light painting. Of course we had to buy another wand, as they play Tag with each other in the dark as well as hide and seek in the dark and casting spells on each other- endless fun for them. I just got one of the wands after bedtime to try a bit of light painting. I only used my camera on the Slow Shutter dial, did not have time to set up a tripod, and snapped a couple photos in the dark with no flash. I caught a photo of the wand making a “V”, and it came out nice for no app or tripod yet. I have seen light painting photos that are fantastic when you know how to manually set your camera for long exposures. Adding a colored cellophane over the light tip makes for gorgeous colored lights too. Our kids love playing with these wands and could care less about the light painting for now. These wands are getting a lot of playtime and are a huge hit- especially with Halloween around the corner. 5 STARS.
text_fidelity_b: WOW! Stuff Collection Fantastic Beasts – Newt’s Light Painting Wand – Award Winner!
